body.statement:
Fix \(n\) and \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).  Let \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\), \(p=2K\), \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\), and
\[
 S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\epsilon_q,
 \qquad
 M_n^Z=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|.
\]
Indexing \(q\) arbitrarily, define the sign-expanded summands
\[
 X_q=\sqrt m\,(a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q,
 -a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,-a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q)\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Every coordinate of \(m^{-1/2}\sum_qX_q\) has variance one, its maximum is \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\), and, for a constant \(C\) depending only on \(C_e\),
\[
 B_n=C\sqrt m\,L_n(K),
 \qquad
 \max_{q,j}\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}\le B_n,
 \qquad
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4\le C mL_n(K)^2.
\]
Consequently, with another constant \(C_1\) depending only on \(C_e\),
\[
 \mathfrak g_n^{(5)}
 =C_1\{L_n(K)^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))\}^{1/4}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|
 \le\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}.
\]
This conclusion permits singular \(\Sigma_n\).

For deterministic \(u\ge0\), define the generic remainder event
\[
 \mathcal R_n(u)=\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le u\}.
\]
For \(h\ge0\), let \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\), set \(\delta_h=2h+h^2\), define \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\), and, when \(h>0\), put
\[
 \mathfrak c_n(h)=C_3\delta_h^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}.
\]
There are constants \(C_2,C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such that whenever \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le \mathfrak g_n^{(5)}+P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}
 +C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), conditionally on \(Y\), \(W_n^\xi\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\), and
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le\mathfrak c_n(h).
\]
If \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}
 \text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\\
 &\quad\le1\wedge\Big[\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}+P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}
 +2P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\hspace{31mm}+C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +2\mathfrak c_n(h)\Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
The formulas remain valid at \(h=0\) by direct substitution.  Therefore, along any complete array in the baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), if deterministic sequences \(u_n,h_n\downarrow0\) obey
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(2p)\to0,
\]
then the multiplier band has simultaneous coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\).  This is conditional on the two displayed probability limits.  Under balanced influence loading \(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), the Gaussian-approximation requirement is exactly the elbow
\[
 \log(Km)=o(m^{1/5}).
\]
body.proof_tex:
By \(s_k^2=\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_q^2\), \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), and \(s_k>0\) from \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\),
\[
 \sum_qa_{kq}^2=1. \tag{1}
\]
The variables \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\) are well defined because \(\sigma_q>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:variance-bounds}\).  They are centered and mutually independent by \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) and \(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\), satisfy \(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^2=1\), and obey \(\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\) by \(\texttt{ass:heteroskedastic-subgaussian}\).  Thus the \(X_q\)'s are independent and centered.  For a coordinate \(j\) associated with horizon \(k\), equation (1) gives
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2
 =\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1. \tag{2}
\]
A sub-Gaussian variable with \(\psi_2\)-norm at most \(C_e\) has fourth moment bounded by a constant depending only on \(C_e\).  Hence
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4
 =m\sum_qa_{kq}^4E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^4
 \le C mL_n(K)^2\sum_qa_{kq}^2
 =C mL_n(K)^2. \tag{3}
\]
Also \(\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}\le C\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_2}\le C\sqrt mL_n(K)\).  Since (1) implies \(1\le mL_n(K)^2\), the choice \(B_n=C\sqrt mL_n(K)\) is at least one after increasing \(C\).  Equations (2)--(3) verify all moment and scale hypotheses of \(\texttt{lem:cckk2022-gaussian-approximation}\) with fixed \(b_1,b_2\).  Its hyperrectangle inequality applied to the lower rectangles \((-\infty,z]^p\), and to the sign-expanded vector, yields
\[
 \sup_z\left|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{B_n^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))}{m}\right\}^{1/4}
 =\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}. \tag{4}
\]
The Gaussian vector in (4) has covariance \(\Sigma_n\) by \(\texttt{lem:staircase-covariance}\).  The cited theorem assumes coordinatewise variance lower bounds, verified by (2), but no positive minimum eigenvalue; thus a singular staircase correlation is allowed.

By the definition of \(\rho_n\), exactly and without a linearization event,
\[
 s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})=S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k}. \tag{5}
\]
Put \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), \(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\) gives \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  If \(\delta_h\le1/2\), then \(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}>0\), and elementary algebra gives
\[
 |t_k^{-1}-1|
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{\sqrt{1-\delta_h}(1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h})}
 \le\delta_h,
 \qquad t_k^{-1}\le\sqrt2. \tag{6}
\]
Combining (5)--(6), on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\cap\mathcal B_n(h)\),
\[
 \left|\max_k|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|-\max_k|S_{n,k}|\right|
 \le\delta_h\max_k|S_{n,k}|+\sqrt2u. \tag{7}
\]

Independence, the sub-Gaussian bound, and (1) imply
\(|S_{n,k}\|_{\psi_2}\le C\) uniformly in \(k\).  A union bound therefore gives, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|>C_4\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}\}\le\delta_h. \tag{8}
\]
On the complementary event, the right side of (7) is at most
\[
 v_n=C_5\{\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}+u\}. \tag{9}
\]
The Gaussian vector has unit coordinate variances.  Therefore \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-anti-concentration}\), applied after sign expansion, gives
\[
 \sup_zP\{|M_n^Z-z|\le v_n\}\le C v_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}. \tag{10}
\]
Sandwich the event in (5) studentized by \(\widehat s_k\) between the linear-score events with thresholds \(z-v_n\) and \(z+v_n\).  Equations (4), (8), and (10), together with the union bound for \(\mathcal R_n(u)^c\) and \(\mathcal B_n(h)^c\), yield the asserted distribution inequality after using, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \delta_h+\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}
 \le C\left[\delta_h\log(2p)
 +\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}\right]. \tag{11}
\]
This elementary inequality follows by splitting \(\log(2p/\delta_h)=\log(2p)+\log(1/\delta_h)\), applying \(2\sqrt{ab}\le a+b\), and using \(x\log(1/x)=o(x^{1/3})\) as \(x\downarrow0\), with the remaining compact interval absorbed into the constant.

Conditionally on \(Y\), independence and Gaussianity of the multipliers give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q,
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_{k'}}\xi_q
 \mathrel{\Big|}Y\right)=\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}. \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi\mid Y\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), the deterministic covariance theorem gives
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}\le4\delta_h. \tag{13}
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-comparison-maxima}\) to the sign-expanded Gaussian vectors proves the asserted conditional comparison bound.  It also requires only marginal variance nondegeneracy, so singular covariance is harmless.

Let \(F_Z\) be the distribution function of \(M_n^Z\).  The anti-concentration bound makes \(F_Z\) continuous.  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), if \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(W_n^\xi\) lies between the \((1-\alpha-\mathfrak c_n(h))\)- and \((1-\alpha+\mathfrak c_n(h))\)-quantiles of \(F_Z\).  Apply the preceding feasible-statistic distribution bound at those two deterministic quantiles and add \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\).  This gives the finite coverage inequality, including its second copies of the score-event probability and \(\mathfrak c_n(h)\).  When \(h=0\), equations (6) and (13) have zero discrepancy, proving the stated direct-substitution convention.

Finally, the corrected \(\texttt{ass:cell-leverage}\) implies \(\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}\to0\).  The two stated probability limits remove the two event failures.  The condition \(u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\) removes the remainder perturbation, and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\) implies both \(\delta_{h_n}\log(2p)\to0\) and \(\mathfrak c_n(h_n)\to0\), using \(x\log^2(1/x)\to0\).  Hence the coverage error tends to zero.  If \(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), then \(L_n(K)^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))\to0\) is equivalent, up to fixed multiplicative constants inside the logarithm, to \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\), which proves the elbow statement.
body.justification: This theorem isolates the universal growing-dimensional step and improves the sufficient leverage condition from log power seven to five without assuming covariance nonsingularity.
body.gap: The theorem deliberately takes the nonlinear remainder event and feasible score event as inputs; generic Gaussian approximation cannot derive their probabilities from matrix-completion geometry.
body.consumer: Researchers obtain an explicit coverage-error certificate and the balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).
